issues.summary: Accept the canonical `LP: #<id>` form the validation regex currently rejects
issues.detail: ci.yaml:172 `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` requires digits immediately after `LP:`, so `Fixes LP: #12345` — the Launchpad-documented form (`LP: #<LP-Bug-Number>`) and the one the PR description says it standardizes on — hard-fails CI, while legacy `LP:123`/`LP: 123` (which Launchpad does not link) pass. Suggested fix: `LP:\s*#?\s*\K[0-9]+` or require the `#`.

issues.summary: Update lp-bug-update.yaml's identical extraction regex in the same commit
issues.detail: .github/workflows/lp-bug-update.yaml:24 keeps the digit-only `LP:\s*\K[0-9]+` pattern and is untouched by this diff; once references adopt `LP: #<id>` the post-merge job logs "No Launchpad bug ID found" and silently stops moving bugs to Fix Committed. The two copies must accept the same format, applied together.

issues.summary: Reconcile PR description with diff: promised work and doc updates are missing
issues.detail: The description promises a repo-wide switch to `LP: #<id>` and writing a comment on the LP bug with the PR/commit link, but the diff only adds one ci.yaml step; `utilities/mark_lp_bug_fix_committed.py` only sets task status, and AGENTS.md (lines 99/131/154) still documents the legacy `Resolves LP:2066936` form, leaving the newly enforced format undocumented. Either the diff is incomplete or the description is stale.

issues.summary: Anchor `LP` with a left word boundary to stop false-positive failures
issues.detail: The outer grep `.*LP:\s*` has no `\b` before `LP`, so case-insensitive matching trips on words like `help:`/`HELP: 42`, `gulp:`, `scalp:` and on Launchpad branch URIs such as `lp:~user/branch` or `lp:maas/+git/maas`, producing spurious CI failures (and the extractor in lp-bug-update.yaml has the same flaw). Use `\bLP:` in both workflows.

issues.summary: Check validates PR body while lp-bug-update parses commit messages
issues.detail: The new step gates `github.event.pull_request.body`, but the consumer extracts bug IDs from `.commits[].message` on push to master; the two agree only under squash-merge-with-PR-body, so with merge/rebase strategies a green check still yields no bug update. State the squash assumption in a comment or validate the PR's commit messages instead.

issues.summary: Handle multi-line references: grep is line-based and `.` never crosses newlines
issues.detail: Both greps operate line-by-line, so the closing keyword and the `LP:` reference must appear on the same line; a body like `Fixes the parser.\n\nLP: #123` silently skips validation (and the same limitation makes lp-bug-update miss it). Normalize the body or use `-z`/`(?s)` if multi-line references are meant to be legal.

issues.summary: Fix error message: it advertises the rejected `LP:<number>` form, give example
issues.detail: ci.yaml:174 tells authors `Expected syntax ... LP:<number>` — the legacy form this change deprecates and that Launchpad does not link — contradicting the PR description and docs. Print the accepted form with a concrete example (e.g. `Expected syntax: Fixes LP: #123456`) and echo the offending line for debuggability.

issues.summary: Detection gate misses the legacy spellings it is meant to catch
issues.detail: The outer gate requires `LP:` to already be present, so `Fixes LP#2066936`, `Fixes LP 2066936`, and `Fixes bug 2066936` skip the check entirely and then silently fail extraction in lp-bug-update.yaml. Detect with something like `${KEYWORDS}.*\bLP\b` and require the full canonical form in the validation step.

issues.summary: Anchor the validated reference to the closing keyword, not the whole body
issues.detail: The inner check on line 172 scans the entire body for any `LP:<digits>` independently of the keyword match, so `Closes LP: <malformed>` plus an unrelated valid `LP: 123` elsewhere still passes; `.*` between keyword and reference allows the same within one line. Validate keyword and adjacent reference in a single anchored regex.

issues.summary: Deduplicate the keyword/format regexes shared with lp-bug-update.yaml
issues.detail: The keyword alternation now exists twice in this step and a third time verbatim in lp-bug-update.yaml:24; the comment "Same keywords as the lp-bug-update workflow" documents a coupling nothing enforces, and the copies already disagree on `#`. Hoist into a shell variable here and extract one shared script under `utilities/` (or composite action) consumed by both workflows.

issues.summary: Check only fires with a closing keyword; bare `fix` PRs escape validation
issues.detail: Despite the step name "Verify Launchpad bug reference", a `fix` PR with no `Fixes/Closes/Resolves` line passes even though AGENTS.md makes a ticket reference mandatory for `fix` commits. Clarify the step's scope or extend validation beyond closing-keyword lines.

issues.summary: Add tests covering the accept/reject matrix of the new validation
issues.detail: No test exists for the new format gate; a small script under `utilities/` with unit tests over cases like `LP: 123`, `LP: #123`, `LP:# 123`, `HELP: 123`, and multi-line bodies would have caught the inverted regex and the duplication drift.

issues.summary: Drop the `\K` in the inner grep: it is a no-op under `-q`
issues.detail: ci.yaml:172 uses `\K` to reset the match start, but with `grep -q` nothing is printed and only match existence matters, so the sequence has no effect (keeping it identical to lp-bug-update.yaml is harmless but technically unnecessary).

issues.summary: Add `edited` to pull_request trigger types so description fixes re-run
issues.detail: ci.yaml's `on.pull_request.types` is `[opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]` with no `edited`; a contributor who fixes the PR description after this check fails gets no re-run until they push. Add `edited` or split description checks into a dedicated workflow.

issues.summary: Remove dead trailing `\s*` from the outer grep pattern
issues.detail: In ci.yaml:171 the trailing `\s*` after `LP:` is dead weight — `.*LP:` is equivalent for an unanchored grep match.
